item.title: Version 9.3.2
item.description:
Version 9.3.2 New

Better

  • Your words land even sooner. PUSHTYPE no longer waits before pasting what you said, which takes about another 0.05 seconds off the moment you let go of the PUSH-to-talk key.

Version 9.3.1

Better

  • Your words land more than twice as fast. Text now appears about 0.13 seconds after you let go of the PUSH-to-talk key, down from about 0.35. The pill's glow was holding the app up for a moment after every dictation, and stopping the microphone now happens in the background.
  • Shorter setup. Seven pages, eight with a license, down from ten. Choose Talk and TYPE on the welcome page; your name, About you, learning and screen choices are now on one page, "Make it yours".
  • Settings, rearranged. TYPE's models now sit in Models beside the speech models, with one Storage section for both. The pill's position and live preview are in Talk.
  • Show my words as I speak can be switched on in setup when you choose Parakeet Streaming.
  • TYPE keeps suggesting while you download a different model, using the one you already have until the new one is ready.
  • Speech models download from a fixed, tested version, so a change upstream can't reach you untested. Models you already have are kept.
  • The menu says what's missing. "Needs Accessibility" or "Needs Microphone", with a Fix button, instead of "Ready" when the key can't work.
  • Diagnostic log in Settings ▸ General, with Show in Finder and Clear, for when you write to support. It never records what you say or type, or which apps you use.
  • Deleting a model asks first. Clearer wording, better VoiceOver labels, calmer animations with Reduce Motion, and tighter spacing throughout.

Fixed

  • Two quick dictations no longer lose your clipboard. The second one used to put the first one's text back on your clipboard instead of what you had copied.
  • TYPE works as soon as you grant Accessibility, without restarting PUSHTYPE.
  • TYPE ignores every key while a password field has secure input on.
  • Turning on the wake word no longer freezes the app for a few seconds while the microphone starts.
  • A Mac with no microphone connected no longer crashes when you press the key.
  • Microphone refused: pressing the key now tells you how to fix it, instead of an alert at every launch.
  • No speech model yet: the key waits for your download instead of starting one on its own.
  • Setup's speech-model download has a Cancel button, and says so when nothing has arrived for 90 seconds.

Version 9.3.0

New

  • Set up a second Mac in a minute. When you open PUSHTYPE on a Mac that shares your iCloud with another, setup starts by asking "Already use PUSHTYPE on another Mac?" Say yes and your settings, dictionary, name and About you come across, and the pages you've already answered are skipped. Each Mac still asks for its own permissions and downloads. Settings ▸ General has a Copy Settings button for later.
  • Share what it learns between your Macs. Switch on "Share what it learns with my other Macs" in Settings ▸ Personal, on each Mac you want it on. It travels through your own iCloud, encrypted with a key only your Apple Account has, and Delete All erases it everywhere. Off by default.
  • Pause learning. Like Pause Type: for an hour or until tomorrow, from the menu bar or Settings ▸ Personal. Nothing you write while paused is kept, including the note you were in the middle of.
  • Setup now covers learning. A new page, "Make it sound like you", asks for your name, an About you note and whether to learn from your writing. The welcome page and the screen page now cover autocomplete, learning and what you copy.

Better

  • Each Mac keeps its own choices. Only your name and About you follow you automatically. Everything else is copied once, when you ask, so a work Mac can stay different. The wake word, models and microphone choices never leave a Mac.

Fixed

  • Dictionary entries for symbols now work. An entry like "&" → "AMP" never fired, because the dictionary needed a letter beside it. It now works for "&", "@" and entries ending in a period, and it catches the symbol when you say the word "ampersand".

Version 9.2.2

Better

  • Going back to fix a word no longer covers your text. In Claude Code and other agent prompts in Terminal, when you move the cursor back into what you've written, the suggestion now appears in a small card below the line, as it already did in other apps, instead of on top of the words after the cursor.
  • No more repeats. A suggestion never repeats the words that are already after your cursor. Going back after "I'm" in "I'm I don't know how…" offers "sure", not "sure I don't know how".

Version 9.2.1

Fixed

  • Password keystrokes are never kept. For the few apps whose text PUSHTYPE can't read, Type remembers the keys you just typed in that field, in memory only. Keys typed into a password field could stay in that memory and, after Tab, be read as the next field's text. Now nothing typed into a password field is kept, the memory clears whenever you move to another field, and Tab clears it too.

Version 9.2.0

Better

  • Spelling fixes catch more typos. The fix stays on offer while you carry on typing the next word ("I will recieve i" → "I will receive i"), so you don't have to stop at the typo. Words you're still typing ("apprec…") are never treated as mistakes.
  • The right word. Fixes now use the same choice as your Mac's own autocorrect, looking at the whole sentence, so "recive" becomes "receive", not "revive".
  • A space after the fix, like an accepted suggestion, when you fix the word you just typed.
  • Spelling fixes in Claude Code and other agent prompts in Terminal. Accept with your whole-suggestion key (` ~); Tab stays the terminal's.

Version 9.1.3

New

  • Type learns your habits. When you finish a phrase the same way again and again ("Thanks for sending this over. I'll take a look tonight."), PUSHTYPE offers your wording as soon as you start it. Habits are learned from everything you write with "Learn from my writing and voice" on, and only after you've written something the same way at least three times, so a one-off detail from one conversation never turns up in another. Past writing on the same topic still comes only from the same window.

Fixed

  • Quitting PUSHTYPE no longer ends in a crash. With a typing model loaded, macOS could report that PUSHTYPE quit unexpectedly every time you quit.

Version 9.1.2

New

  • Type fixes typos. When the word you just typed is misspelled, the gray text shows the correction, like → receive. Press your accept key (Tab) and PUSHTYPE swaps it in, then carries on suggesting. Corrections come from your Mac's own spell checker, offline. Turn it off in Settings ▸ Typing ▸ Offer spelling fixes.

Version 9.1.1

Fixed

  • Type works in Webex. With Webex in front, PUSHTYPE couldn't find the message box, so there was no Type icon and no suggestions. It now finds the box in Webex and in other apps built the same way.

Changed

  • Extra Macs are $12 on the license screen, matching checkout.
  • Legal notices now include llama.cpp's license, which Type is built on, and the terms use the PUSHTYPE name.

Version 9.1.0

New

  • PUSH is now PUSHTYPE. Same app, new name, for voice and typing. Your settings, permissions and downloaded models carry over.
  • Choose your accept keys. In Settings ▸ Typing, pick the key that takes the next word (Tab by default) and the one that takes the whole suggestion (the ` ~ key by default). Keys you need for writing, like Return, Space and Esc, can't be used, and PUSHTYPE says why.
  • Suggestion color in the menu. Switch colors straight from the menu bar when gray is hard to see on a see-through field or a busy wallpaper.
  • Learn from my writing and voice. What you dictate where suggestions are on is learned too, as finished text and never audio. It's still off until you turn it on, encrypted, and only on this Mac.
  • Screen Recording gets its own welcome page, explaining what it reads and that nothing is kept. If macOS asks to quit and reopen PUSHTYPE after you allow it, the welcome window comes back on the same page.
  • Downloaded typing models show how much space they use, with Show in Finder.

Changed

  • Type is on by default, like Dictation. Until a typing model is downloaded, the menu says where to get one.
  • A shorter welcome: two pages fewer. The pill's position is chosen on the Try it page, and the wake word and teleprompter are on the last page.
  • Settings: the Text page's options (formatting, spoken corrections, California mode) are now in Dictation. The Dictionary says up front that it's used for both voice and typing.
  • The smallest typing model (Qwen3.5 0.8B) is gone. If you used it, PUSHTYPE switches to Recommended.

Fixed

  • The menu's arrow stays on the icon when the icon changes, for example from the hourglass once the typing model is ready.

Version 9.0.0

New

  • Type. As you type in any app, PUSH suggests how your sentence goes on, in gray right at the cursor. Press Tab to take it a word at a time, or keep typing to ignore it. It works in Mail, Notes, Messages, TextEdit, web pages in Safari and Chrome, and Claude Code in Terminal. Like dictation, it runs entirely on this Mac: nothing you type leaves it.
  • Suggestions right after dictation. Finish a dictated sentence and the next suggestion appears on its own, space included.
  • Pick your model. Four sizes, from Qwen3.5 0.8B (630 MB) to Gemma 4 E4B (5.3 GB, for Macs with 16 GB or more). Bigger models write better; smaller ones are lighter on memory. Change it any time in Settings ▸ Typing.
  • Make it yours. Choose the suggestion length and color, add a sign-off name and a note about how you write, and turn Type off in the apps where you don't want it. Words in your PUSH Dictionary finish themselves and are never treated as typos.
  • Learn from my writing (Settings ▸ Personal, off by default). PUSH keeps what you write, encrypted and only on this Mac, and uses it so suggestions sound like you. Never synced; Delete All erases it.
  • Context helps. What you just copied and the text around the field shape the suggestion. Neither is ever stored. Both can be turned off in Settings ▸ Typing.
  • Choose your features. Dictation and Type can each be switched on or off, in the welcome window, in Settings, and in the menu.

Changed

  • New icon: a microphone over a keyboard, for voice and typing.
  • The menu bar symbol shows what's on: a microphone for Dictation, a text cursor for Type.
  • In the menu, "Model" is now "Voice".

Fixed

  • Clicking the menu bar icon again closes the menu.

Version 8.2.8

New

  • Drag to allow Accessibility. When PUSH sends you to System Settings for Accessibility, a PUSH card now rides along at the bottom of the window. Drag PUSH from the card into the list and you're done: no hunting for the + button, no digging through Applications. The card follows the window, steps aside when you switch apps, and goes away by itself the moment access is on. The push-to-talk key starts working straight away, no restart needed.

Version 8.2.7

New

  • Pick your start sound (Settings ▸ Dictation). Six sounds made for PUSH: Deep Tap (the new default), Mic Tap, Bright Tap, Key Up, and two 8-bit ones, Power On and Ready. Choosing one plays it. They replace the old radio chirp.

Fixed

  • California mode and numbers. "Like 30 minutes" still means *about* 30 and keeps its "like", but "like 90s themes" and "like 8-bit" now lose it: a decade or a style isn't a quantity.

Version 8.2.6

Fixed

  • "Like I said" and "he was like, no way" keep their "like". PUSH's filler cleanup was removing it, pasting "I said, we're done" and "He was , no way". It now leaves a "like" that's doing a job, with or without California mode.
  • Times said as words. "Four thirty PM" pastes as "4:30 p.m.", not "34 p.m.".

Version 8.2.5

Changed

  • A simpler choice of speech models. PUSH now offers three: Parakeet Streaming, Parakeet Ultra and Nemotron Multilingual. Parakeet Unified is gone. With PUSH transcribing while you talk, it was no faster and no more accurate than Ultra, and it only did English. If you used it, PUSH switches you to the recommended model, and its 600 MB download is removed to free the space.
  • The recommended model follows your Mac's language. On an English Mac it's Parakeet Streaming, which shows your words in the pill as you speak. Anywhere else it's Parakeet Ultra, which understands English and the European languages and switches between them on its own. You can still pick any model in Settings ▸ Models.

Version 8.2.4

Faster

  • Long dictation lands almost instantly. PUSH now transcribes finished sentences while you're still talking, so letting go leaves only your last sentence or two. On a 25-second dictation, the wait after you let go drops from about a quarter of a second to a few hundredths.

Fixed

  • "I mean" without a pause. "15.2 seconds I mean 1.52 seconds" now pastes as "1.52 seconds" even when you don't pause before "I mean".
  • Times of day. "4:30 pm" and "4:30 PM" paste as "4:30 p.m.", like the rest of PUSH.

Version 8.2.3

Fixed

  • Long dictation keeps its punctuation. Past about 15 seconds, PUSH sometimes stopped adding full stops, commas and capitals partway through, so everything after that point also missed its cleanup. PUSH now splits long dictation where a sentence ends, which keeps the punctuation all the way through. On Parakeet Unified, the first word after each split is no longer dropped either.
  • "New paragraph" after a quote. Saying "new line" or "new paragraph" right after "end quote" now breaks the line instead of typing the words.
  • Money in words. "Five million dollars" pastes as $5 million, not $5,000,000.
  • Doubled full stops. "seconds.." pastes as "seconds.". A real "..." is left alone.
  • California mode. "Could you like send it" now drops the "like"; "would you like to come" and "I like cooking" keep theirs.

Version 8.2.2

New

  • Lay out text by voice. Say "new line" or "new paragraph" where you pause and PUSH breaks the line. Say "bullet point" before each item for a bulleted list.
  • Numbered lists. "Number one, milk. Number two, eggs." pastes as 1. Milk and 2. Eggs on their own lines. It only becomes a list when the numbers count up from one, so "we're number one" stays a sentence.
  • Rank your microphones (Settings ▸ Dictation). Add the mics you use in the order you prefer; PUSH records from the first one that's connected, and switches as soon as you plug one in.
  • Closed-lid mode. With your MacBook's lid shut, PUSH skips the built-in microphone, which records silence when the lid is closed, and uses a real one instead.
  • What's new, right here. Update notes now show in this window, with the last few versions below.

Changed

  • The single microphone choice is now a list. If you had picked one, add it again in Settings ▸ Dictation.

Version 8.2.1

New

  • Choose your speech model during setup. On first launch, the welcome wizard now has a "Choose a speech model" step. Parakeet Ultra is selected and recommended. Press Download, watch the progress, and continue once the model is ready. Setup can't be skipped until a model is on your Mac, since PUSH can't dictate without one.

Changed

  • PUSH no longer downloads a speech model silently at first launch. The 600 MB download now happens only when you choose it, in setup or in Settings ▸ Models. The small supporting models still load automatically.

Version 8.2.0

New

  • California mode (Settings ▸ Text, off by default). Removes casual "like": "It was like really good" → "It was really good." Keeps "I like it", "looks like rain", "like I said", "like 30 minutes" and "he was like, no way."

Changed

  • Apple Speech has been removed. It was the least accurate engine in every benchmark. The models are now Parakeet Ultra (default), Parakeet Unified, Parakeet Streaming and Nemotron Multilingual. If Apple Speech was your choice, PUSH switches to Parakeet Ultra.

Fixed

  • Emphasis isn't treated as a correction. "It's cold, I mean very cold." used to paste as "Very cold."
  • "Scratch that" no longer leaves a stray period at the start of the next sentence.
  • Corrected numbers are replaced whole. "The budget is 5 million. Sorry, 6 million." → "The budget is 6 million."
  • A question after a quote gets its "?". Priya said, "Ship it anyway." Can you confirm before Friday?
  • Quotes after "said," start with a capital. Priya said, "Ship it anyway."

Version 8.1.3

  • Spoken self-corrections are on by default: "15.2 seconds, I mean 1.52 seconds" pastes as "1.52 seconds". Turn it off in Settings ▸ Text.
  • Missing question marks: when the model leaves a question unpunctuated ("…Can you confirm before Friday"), PUSH adds the "?" — including right after a quotation.
  • Quotes after "said,": Priya said, quote, ship it anyway, end quote → Priya said, "Ship it anyway."
  • Capital after a removed filler: "…target. Um, latency…" → "…target. Latency…"
  • Numbers with units stay numbers: "at 1.52 seconds" or "by 2.25 percent" no longer turn into clock times.
  • Spacing: a correction in a later sentence no longer glues it to the sentence before.

Version 8.1.2

  • Decimals in self-corrections: "latency came back at 15.2 seconds, I mean 1.52 seconds" now resolves to "…1.52 seconds" instead of garbling into "15. 1. 52 seconds". (Only applies with spoken self-corrections switched on.)
  • Fillers mid-text: an "Um," that opens a later sentence is now removed, not just one at the very start.
  • "Umbrella" is safe: text starting with words like "Umbrella" no longer loses its first letters to the filler remover.

Version 8.1.1

  • Corrections across a sentence break: "…send a letter to Sarah? I mean John." → "…send a letter to John?"; "…at eight o'clock. I mean four o'clock." → "…at four o'clock." Only when the short fix clearly matches the end of the previous sentence (a name for a name, a number for a number).
  • Parakeet Unified and Streaming are separate downloads: deleting one no longer deletes the other, and each shows its own size.

Version 8.1.0

Everything since 8.0.2, now on the default Parakeet Ultra:

  • Spoken corrections are stricter and smarter. "Tuesday, sorry, Wednesday" → Wednesday; "It costs 20, correction, 25 dollars" → 25 dollars; "before 7.0. 8.0, sorry." → before 8.0. Everyday phrases ("I mean," to start a sentence, "Sorry for the delay", "delete that file") are no longer touched, and long sentences after "I mean" no longer delete what came before.
  • Parakeet Ultra is the default — English plus the Latin-script European languages, detected automatically. Nemotron Multilingual covers the rest.
  • Spoken quotes — "quote … end quote", "quote unquote", and a "quote" that closes itself at the end of the sentence.
  • Clock times written as 3:30.
  • Parakeet TDT v2 removed; FluidAudio updated to 0.17.4.
